components.note: 纟 (silk, simplified 糸) — thread that draws in; also in 红 red, 级 level.
宿 (sù) gives a close sound; it also appears in 宿舍 dormitory.
小 (small) — three small dots, tiny grains. As a radical it appears in 少 few, 尖 sharp.

example.hanzi: 这张图片可以缩小尺寸。
example.pinyin: zhè zhāng túpiàn kěyǐ suōxiǎo chǐcùn.
example.english: This image's size can be reduced.
example.fact: The Aral Sea, once the world's fourth-largest lake, has shrunk to roughly a tenth of its original size since the 1960s after Soviet irrigation projects diverted the rivers that fed it — the exposed seabed is now a salt-and-dust desert known as the Aralkum.

examples.hanzi: 请把照片缩小一点,再发给我。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ zhàopiàn suōxiǎo yìdiǎn, zài fā gěi wǒ.
examples.english: Please shrink the photo a bit before sending it to me.

examples.hanzi: 两个城市的差距正在缩小。
examples.pinyin: Liǎng gè chéngshì de chājù zhèngzài suōxiǎo.
examples.english: The gap between the two cities is shrinking.

components.note: 虍 (tiger head) — the top of 虎; it also appears in 虑 lǜ and 虐 nüè, but in 虚 the link to tigers is lost.
木 (wood) — 木 is wood, as in 桌, 板; 构 first meant framing with timber.
勾 (gōu) — near sound — 构 is gòu; 勾 also sounds out 沟 gōu, 购 gòu and 够 gòu.

example.hanzi: 这个故事完全是虚构的。
example.pinyin: zhège gùshi wánquán shì xūgòu de.
example.english: This story is entirely fictional.
example.fact: In 1938, Orson Welles' radio adaptation of H.G. Wells' novel The War of the Worlds was presented as a series of simulated news bulletins about a Martian invasion — although reports of mass panic were later found to be exaggerated by newspapers, the broadcast remains one of the most famous examples of fiction blurring with perceived reality.

examples.hanzi: 这部小说的人物都是作者虚构的。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bù xiǎoshuō de rénwù dōu shì zuòzhě xūgòu de.
examples.english: The characters in this novel were all made up by the author.

examples.hanzi: 你不要虚构事实,说真话。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ bú yào xūgòu shìshí, shuō zhēnhuà.
examples.english: Don't fabricate facts; tell the truth.

meanings: the limit of what one is prepared to accept

components.note: 广 (shelter) — buildings, as in 店 shop, 床 bed, 度 degree; 底 is the base of a house.
氐 (dī) is a close sound clue for dǐ; also in 低 dī and 抵 dǐ.
纟 (thread, simplified 糸) — silk and cord: 红, 给, 组; 线 is thread or line.
戋 (jiān) is a loose sound clue; same part in 浅 qiǎn, 钱 qián and 残 cán.

example.hanzi: 诚实是他做人的底线。
example.pinyin: chéngshí shì tā zuò rén de dǐxiàn.
example.english: Honesty is his bottom line as a person.
example.fact: In 168 BC, Roman envoy Gaius Popillius Laenas drew a line in the sand around Seleucid king Antiochus IV and demanded he decide whether to withdraw from Egypt before stepping outside it — the ultimatum worked, and the phrase 'line in the sand' still describes a firm limit today.

examples.hanzi: 做生意要有底线,不能骗人。
examples.pinyin: Zuò shēngyi yào yǒu dǐxiàn, bù néng piàn rén.
examples.english: In business you must have a bottom line; you can't cheat people.

examples.hanzi: 他一个球打到了底线外。
examples.pinyin: Tā yí gè qiú dǎdàole dǐxiàn wài.
examples.english: He hit the ball beyond the baseline.

components.note: 亻 (person) — person radical — 传 is something passed from person to person.
专 (zhuān) — near sound — 传 is chuán; 专 also sounds out 转 zhuǎn and 砖 zhuān.
辶 (walk, 走之旁) — movement and roads: 过, 进, 送; 达 is to get through to, to reach.
大 (dà) is only a loose stand-in for the old sound part, so treat it as a rough clue for dá.

example.hanzi: 他把老师的话传达给了全班同学。
example.pinyin: Tā bǎ lǎoshī de huà chuándá gěi le quánbān tóngxué.
example.english: He conveyed the teacher's words to the whole class.
example.fact: The Pony Express relayed mail across nearly 2,000 miles of the American West in about 10 days, with riders swapping fresh horses every 10-15 miles — a relay system that beat the stagecoach by more than half. It shut down in 1861 almost as soon as the transcontinental telegraph could convey messages across the same distance in minutes instead of days.

examples.hanzi: 请把我的谢意传达给你的父母。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ wǒ de xièyì chuándá gěi nǐ de fùmǔ.
examples.english: Please convey my thanks to your parents.

examples.hanzi: 这首歌想传达一种温暖的感觉。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shǒu gē xiǎng chuándá yì zhǒng wēnnuǎn de gǎnjué.
examples.english: This song tries to convey a warm feeling.

components.note: 人 (person) — the right-hand part. The left part is a hook-and-dot, from an old tool-like shape. Meaning 'by means of, so as to' is not shown by the parts today.
Memory aid: a person 人 using a tool to get something done — 'by means of' (可以, 所以, 以前). A mnemonic, not proven etymology.
⺈ (bent person) — a person's figure, the top part of 色. Old story: a person (⺈) sitting on 巴 shows how feelings colour the face, hence 'colour, look'; treat as a memory aid.
巴 (bā) — the lower part; dictionary reads the pair as 'what a person desires'. Memory aid: a face reddening with feeling is a 'colour'.
刂 (knife) — marks cutting and dividing, as in 别, 刻, 划; 列 is to split into rows, hence a line or list.
歹 (bone, death) — marks death and decay, as in 死, 残; 列 liè itself also sounds out 烈 liè and 裂 liè.

example.hanzi: 以色列位于中东地区。
example.pinyin: Yǐsèliè wèiyú Zhōngdōng dìqū.
example.english: Israel is located in the Middle East region.
example.fact: The Dead Sea, on Israel's border, sits about 430 meters below sea level — the lowest point on Earth's land surface. Its water is roughly ten times saltier than the ocean, which is why swimmers float on the surface almost without trying.

examples.hanzi: 我朋友去年去以色列旅行了两个星期。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ péngyou qùnián qù Yǐsèliè lǚxíngle liǎng gè xīngqī.
examples.english: My friend traveled to Israel for two weeks last year.

examples.hanzi: 以色列的橙子又大又甜。
examples.pinyin: Yǐsèliè de chéngzi yòu dà yòu tián.
examples.english: Israel's oranges are big and sweet.

components.note: 虫 (insect) — marks insects, as in 蜂 bee, 蚊 mosquito, 蜘 spider; 蜜 is what bees make: honey.
宓 (mì) gives the sound exactly: 蜜 mì, also in 密 mì.

example.hanzi: 我喜欢在茶里加蜂蜜。
example.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuan zài chá lǐ jiā fēngmì.
example.english: I like to add honey to my tea.
example.fact: 蜜 is honey: 蜂蜜. A bee is 蜜蜂 (honey bee), the same two characters in the other order. 蜜月 is honeymoon, and 甜蜜 describes sweetness in a relationship; 蜜饯 is candied fruit.

examples.hanzi: 这种蜂蜜非常甜。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng fēngmì fēicháng tián.
examples.english: This kind of honey is very sweet.

examples.hanzi: 他们是一对甜蜜的小夫妻。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen shì yí duì tiánmì de xiǎo fūqī.
examples.english: They are a sweet young couple.

components.note: 艹 (grass) — plant radical, as in 花 flower, 草 grass; 薄 first meant a thicket.
溥 (pǔ) is a loose clue; its right part 尃 also sounds out 博 bó and 簿 bù.

example.hanzi: 这本书很薄。
example.pinyin: Zhè běn shū hěn báo.
example.english: This book is very thin.
example.fact: 薄 is the opposite of 厚 and describes flat things such as books or clothes. In compounds it is read bó, as in 薄弱 (weak), 淡薄 (faint), 刻薄 (mean). 薄荷 (mint) is read bòhe.

examples.hanzi: 今天风大，你穿得太薄了。
examples.pinyin: Jīntiān fēng dà, nǐ chuān de tài báo le.
examples.english: It is windy today, and you are dressed too thinly.

examples.hanzi: 他把面团擀得很薄。
examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ miàntuán gǎn de hěn báo.
examples.english: He cut the dough very thin.

components.note: 钅 (metal; traditional 金) — marks metals and metal objects, as in 钟 bell/clock, 钱 money; 铃 is a small metal bell.
令 (lìng) — close sound: 铃 líng. 令 also sounds out 零 líng and 龄 líng.

example.hanzi: 下课铃响了。
example.pinyin: Xiàkè líng xiǎng le.
example.english: The bell for the end of class rang.
example.fact: 铃 is a small bell: 门铃 (doorbell), 铃声 (ringtone or bell sound), 车铃 (bicycle bell), 哑铃 (dumbbell, literally "mute bell"). In Japanese names, 铃木 is Suzuki.

examples.hanzi: 我的手机铃声太小了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de shǒujī língshēng tài xiǎo le.
examples.english: My phone's ringtone is too quiet.

examples.hanzi: 有人在门外按门铃。
examples.pinyin: Yǒu rén zài mén wài àn ménlíng.
examples.english: Someone is ringing the doorbell outside.

components.note: 禾 (grain) — marks grain and crops, as in 种, 秋; 税 is tax, originally paid in grain.
兑 (duì) — loose sound hint (shuì); same part in 说 shuō and 脱 tuō.

example.hanzi: 你要交多少税？
example.pinyin: Nǐ yào jiāo duōshao shuì?
example.english: How much tax do you have to pay?
example.fact: 税 is tax: 交税 (to pay tax), 个人所得税 (personal income tax, shortened to 个税), 关税 (customs duty), 免税 (duty-free), 增值税 (VAT).

examples.hanzi: 商品价格已经含税了。
examples.pinyin: Shāngpǐn jiàgé yǐjīng hán shuì le.
examples.english: The price of the goods already includes tax.

examples.hanzi: 公司每年都要交税。
examples.pinyin: Gōngsī měinián dōu yào jiāoshuì.
examples.english: The company has to pay taxes every year.

components.note: 禾 (grain) — grain radical — 程 first meant to measure grain, hence standard, then course and journey; also in 种, 秋, 稿.
呈 (chéng) — same sound — 程 is chéng; 呈 also sounds out 逞 chěng.

example.hanzi: 我们先看一下今天的行程。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen xiān kàn yíxià jīntiān de xíngchéng.
example.english: Let's first look at today's itinerary.
example.fact: 程 started as a measure or standard and extended to a stage of a journey or process: 行程 (itinerary), 路程 (distance), 过程 (process), 课程 (course), 工程 (engineering project), 程序 (program), 程序员 (programmer).

examples.hanzi: 这趟旅行的行程很满。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tàng lǚxíng de xíngchéng hěn mǎn.
examples.english: The itinerary for this trip is packed.

examples.hanzi: 他是一名软件工程师。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì yì míng ruǎnjiàn gōngchéngshī.
examples.english: He is a software engineer.

components.note: 钅 (metal) — 钅 is the simplified 金 (metal), as in 钱, 铁; 镇 first meant to weigh down with metal.
真 (zhēn) — near sound — 镇 is zhèn; 真 also sounds out 慎 shèn and 填 tián.
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家 home, 安 safe, 客 guest; settling down under a roof.
正 (zhèng, upright; the lower part is written 疋) is a loose sound clue for dìng; also in 证 zhèng and 政 zhèng.

example.hanzi: 面对危险，她表现得非常镇定。
example.pinyin: Miànduì wēixiǎn, tā biǎoxiàn de fēicháng zhèndìng.
example.english: Facing danger, she remained very calm.
example.fact: Elite free-divers train to stay calm underwater by triggering the mammalian dive reflex, which can slow the human heart rate from a resting ~70 beats per minute to below 20. The reflex, shared with seals and whales, redirects blood to the heart and brain to conserve oxygen during a breath-hold.

examples.hanzi: 越是着急,越要保持镇定。
examples.pinyin: Yuè shì zháojí, yuè yào bǎochí zhèndìng.
examples.english: The more anxious you are, the more you need to stay calm.

examples.hanzi: 他很镇定地回答了所有问题。
examples.pinyin: Tā hěn zhèndìng de huídále suǒyǒu wèntí.
examples.english: He answered all the questions calmly.

components.note: 门 (gate, door) — 门 is a gate, as in 开, 关, 问; 阁 is a pavilion with doors.
各 (gè) — same sound — 阁 is gé; 各 also sounds out 格 gé and 胳 gē.
木 (wood) — 木 is wood and trees, as in 树, 板, 桌; buildings with floors were built of wood, hence 楼.
娄 (lóu) — same sound — 楼 is lóu; 娄 also sounds out 搂 lǒu.

example.hanzi: 我们把旧家具放在阁楼里。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen bǎ jiù jiājù fàng zài gélóu lǐ.
example.english: We put the old furniture in the attic.
example.fact: During World War II, Anne Frank and seven others hid for two years in a cramped attic annex above an Amsterdam canal-house office, accessible only through a door hidden behind a swinging bookcase. Anne's diary, kept there, has since been translated into more than 70 languages.

examples.hanzi: 阁楼里堆满了灰尘和旧箱子。
examples.pinyin: Gélóu lǐ duīmǎnle huīchén hé jiù xiāngzi.
examples.english: The attic is piled with dust and old boxes.

examples.hanzi: 他在阁楼上布置了一间小书房。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài gélóu shàng bùzhìle yì jiān xiǎo shūfáng.
examples.english: He set up a small study in the loft.

meanings: to greet sb by word or action

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 拿, 抱, 把; 打 is to hit.
丁 (dīng) is a loose sound clue for dǎ; 丁 also sounds out 订 dìng, 顶 dǐng and 钉 dīng.
扌 (hand) — hand radical — 招 is to beckon with the hand.
召 (zhào) — near sound — 招 is zhāo; 召 also sounds out 照 zhào and 超 chāo.
口 (mouth) — breath and speech: 吸, 叫, 喊; 呼 is to breathe out or call.
乎 (hū) sounds exactly like 呼.

example.hanzi: 邻居见面都会打招呼。
example.pinyin: Línjū jiànmiàn dōu huì dǎ zhāohu.
example.english: Neighbors greet each other when they meet.
example.fact: Ancient Greek funerary reliefs from the 5th century BC already depict figures clasping right hands, one of the earliest known artistic records of the handshake. One theory holds the gesture proved a person wasn't concealing a weapon, turning a safety check into a lasting greeting.

examples.hanzi: 早上在电梯里遇见老板,我赶紧打招呼。
examples.pinyin: Zǎoshang zài diàntī lǐ yùjiàn lǎobǎn, wǒ gǎnjǐn dǎ zhāohu.
examples.english: I met my boss in the elevator this morning and quickly greeted him.

examples.hanzi: 要请假的话,请先跟我打招呼。
examples.pinyin: Yào qǐngjià dehuà, qǐng xiān gēn wǒ dǎ zhāohu.
examples.english: If you need to take leave, please let me know first.

components.note: 木 (tree) — marks trees and wood, as in 林, 树, 桥; a village among the trees.
寸 (cùn) hints at the sound: 村 cūn is close.
广 (building, shelter) — houses and rooms, as in 店 shop, 床 bed, 座 seat. 庄 is pronounced like 壮 zhuàng and 装 zhuāng, from the traditional 莊.

example.hanzi: 这个村庄坐落在山脚下。
example.pinyin: Zhège cūnzhuāng zuòluò zài shānjiǎo xià.
example.english: This village sits at the foot of a mountain.
example.fact: The town of Jericho, in the Jordan Valley, has archaeological evidence of continuous habitation stretching back more than 11,000 years, making it one of the oldest known permanently inhabited settlements on Earth. Its famous stone tower, dated to around 8000 BC, still predates the pyramids by millennia.

examples.hanzi: 我外婆住在一个很安静的小村庄里。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ wàipó zhù zài yí gè hěn ānjìng de xiǎo cūnzhuāng lǐ.
examples.english: My grandmother lives in a very quiet little village.

examples.hanzi: 这个村庄的人大多靠种田为生。
examples.pinyin: Zhège cūnzhuāng de rén dàduō kào zhòngtián wéi shēng.
examples.english: Most people in this village make a living from farming.

components.note: 扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — actions by hand: 打, 拉, 抱; here a hand seizing someone to pass judgment.
卩 (kneeling person) — with 又 hand: sentencing a kneeling prisoner, then answering back: repay, report.
寸 (hand, inch) — traditional 導 had 道 (road) plus 寸 (hand): a hand leading along a road; 道 dào is also a near-sound clue for 导 dǎo.

example.hanzi: 记者报导了这次事故的经过。
example.pinyin: Jìzhě bàodǎo le zhè cì shìgù de jīngguò.
example.english: The reporter reported on how the accident unfolded.
example.fact: Washington Post reporters Bob Woodward and Carl Bernstein spent two years, from 1972 to 1974, piecing together the Watergate scandal from anonymous sources and leaked documents. Their reporting eventually helped force President Richard Nixon's resignation, the only time a US president has left office that way.

examples.hanzi: 新闻报导说,明天会有大雪。
examples.pinyin: Xīnwén bàodǎo shuō, míngtiān huì yǒu dàxuě.
examples.english: The news report says there will be heavy snow tomorrow.

examples.hanzi: 这篇报导写得很客观。
examples.pinyin: Zhè piān bàodǎo xiě de hěn kèguān.
examples.english: This report is written very objectively.

components.note: 阝 (mound, hill) — left-side 阝 is 阜 (mound), as in 阳, 院; 阿 first meant a slope.
可 (kě) — near sound — 阿 is ā; 可 also sounds out 河 hé and 哥 gē.
宀 (roof) — a house, as in 家 home, 安 safe, 完; 富 is a house full of goods, hence rich.
畐 (fú) gives the sound: 富 fù is close, as in 福 fú and 副 fù.
氵 (water) — sweat is water of the body; also in 河 river, 汤 soup.
干 (gān) is a loose clue; it also sounds out 旱 hàn and 焊 hàn.

example.hanzi: 阿富汗是一个多山的国家。
example.pinyin: Āfùhàn shì yī gè duōshān de guójiā.
example.english: Afghanistan is a mountainous country.
example.fact: The Sar-e-Sang mines in Afghanistan's Badakhshan province have produced lapis lazuli, a deep-blue semi-precious stone, for over 6,000 years. Ground into pigment, that lapis traveled along ancient trade routes to color the eyes of Egyptian pharaohs' masks and, later, European Renaissance paintings.

examples.hanzi: 我在新闻里看到了关于阿富汗的报道。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zài xīnwén lǐ kàndàole guānyú Āfùhàn de bàodào.
examples.english: I saw a report about Afghanistan on the news.

examples.hanzi: 阿富汗的冬天很冷,山上常常有雪。
examples.pinyin: Āfùhàn de dōngtiān hěn lěng, shān shàng chángcháng yǒu xuě.
examples.english: Winters in Afghanistan are cold, and there's often snow in the mountains.

components.note: 氵 (water) — water and liquids, as in 河, 海, 汤: clear water.
青 (qīng) gives the exact sound; also 请 qǐng, 情 qíng, 晴 qíng and 精 jīng.
日 (sun) — brightness and clarity; also in 明 bright, 晴 sunny.
析 (xī) gives the exact sound.

example.hanzi: 这张照片非常清晰。
example.pinyin: Zhè zhāng zhàopiàn fēicháng qīngxī.
example.english: This photo is very clear.
example.fact: The human eye can resolve detail down to roughly 60 pixels per degree of vision, a benchmark display makers call 'retina' resolution. A clear image viewed at typical reading distance on a modern phone screen already exceeds what the eye alone can distinguish.

examples.hanzi: 他的发音很清晰,大家都听得懂。
examples.pinyin: Tā de fāyīn hěn qīngxī, dàjiā dōu tīng de dǒng.
examples.english: His pronunciation is clear, so everyone can understand.

examples.hanzi: 我对那天的事情记得很清晰。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ duì nà tiān de shìqing jì de hěn qīngxī.
examples.english: I remember that day's events very clearly.

components.note: 主 (master, host) — a lamp with a flame on top; a lamp stand was the centre of the room. 主 also sounds out 注 zhù, 住 zhù and 柱 zhù.
攵 (tap, hand with stick) — actions applied to people: 放, 改, 政; 教 is to teach, traditionally with a rod.
孝 (xiào) is a near sound match for jiào; also in 酵 jiào.

example.hanzi: 主教在教堂主持了婚礼。
example.pinyin: Zhǔjiào zài jiàotáng zhǔchí le hūnlǐ.
example.english: The bishop officiated the wedding at the church.
example.fact: St. Nicholas of Myra, a 4th-century bishop in what is now Turkey, was renowned for secretly giving gifts to the poor, including reportedly dropping coins down chimneys and into shoes. Centuries of retelling across Europe eventually reshaped that generous bishop into the modern figure of Santa Claus.

examples.hanzi: 主教在圣诞节的晚上给大家祝福。
examples.pinyin: Zhǔjiào zài Shèngdàn jié de wǎnshang gěi dàjiā zhùfú.
examples.english: The bishop gave everyone blessings on Christmas night.

examples.hanzi: 这座教堂的主教已经工作了三十年。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zuò jiàotáng de zhǔjiào yǐjīng gōngzuòle sānshí nián.
examples.english: The bishop of this church has been working for thirty years.

components.note: 氵 (water) — water, as in 河, 海, 清: in the old form 灋, water stood for fairness, so law and method.
木 (tree) — wood, as in 桌, 树, 板: 案 is a wooden table.
安 (ān) is a close sound clue for àn; also in 按 àn.

example.hanzi: 国会正在讨论这项法案。
example.pinyin: Guóhuì zhèngzài tǎolùn zhè xiàng fǎ'àn.
example.english: Congress is discussing this bill.
example.fact: The Magna Carta, sealed by King John of England in 1215, was drafted to limit a monarch's power and guarantee certain legal rights to nobles. Though most of its specific clauses are now obsolete, its principle that even a ruler is bound by law underlies how modern bills and constitutions are written.

examples.hanzi: 这项法案得到了大多数议员的支持。
examples.pinyin: Zhè xiàng fǎ'àn dédàole dàduōshù yìyuán de zhīchí.
examples.english: This bill won the support of most legislators.

examples.hanzi: 新的法案将在明年开始实行。
examples.pinyin: Xīn de fǎ'àn jiāng zài míngnián kāishǐ shíxíng.
examples.english: The new bill will take effect next year.

components.note: 氵 (water) — marks rivers and water, as in 河, 海, 江; 汉 is the Han River, which gave name to the Han dynasty and people.
土 (earth) — ground and land: 地, 场, 块; city walls were made of earth.
成 (chéng) sounds exactly like 城; also in 诚 chéng and 盛 chéng.

example.hanzi: 汉城是首尔的旧称。
example.pinyin: Hànchéng shì Shǒu'ěr de jiùchēng.
example.english: Hanseong is the old name for Seoul.
example.fact: Seoul has served as a capital city on the banks of the Han River for more than 600 years, since the Joseon Dynasty established it as its capital in 1394. Today the Seoul metropolitan area is home to over 25 million people, roughly half of South Korea's entire population.

examples.hanzi: 他的爷爷小时候住在汉城。
examples.pinyin: Tā de yéye xiǎoshíhou zhù zài Hànchéng.
examples.english: His grandfather lived in Hanseong as a child.

examples.hanzi: 这本旧书里,汉城指的就是今天的首尔。
examples.pinyin: Zhè běn jiù shū lǐ, Hànchéng zhǐ de jiù shì jīntiān de Shǒu'ěr.
examples.english: In this old book, Hanseong refers to today's Seoul.

components.note: 京 (jīng, high mound, capital) is a loose sound clue for jiù; going up to a high place fits 就 "to approach, to go to".
纟 (silk, thread) — simplified 糸 — 绪 first meant the end of a thread, then the clue, as in 头绪, and mood, as in 情绪.
者 (zhě) — loose hint — 绪 is xù.

example.hanzi: 系统已经准备就绪。
example.pinyin: Xìtǒng yǐjīng zhǔnbèi jiùxù.
example.english: The system is ready.
example.fact: During Apollo 11's 1969 launch sequence, NASA's countdown ran through a strict checklist confirming every system — fuel, guidance, telemetry — was ready before the final 'T-minus' seconds ticked to zero. That countdown procedure, refined across earlier Mercury and Gemini missions, became the template still used for rocket launches today.

examples.hanzi: 行李已经打好包,一切准备就绪。
examples.pinyin: Xíngli yǐjīng dǎhǎo bāo, yíqiè zhǔnbèi jiùxù.
examples.english: The luggage is packed and everything is ready.

examples.hanzi: 各位选手就绪后,比赛就开始了。
examples.pinyin: Gèwèi xuǎnshǒu jiùxù hòu, bǐsài jiù kāishǐ le.
examples.english: Once all contestants are ready, the race begins.

components.note: 扌 (hand, 提手旁) — marks hand actions, as in 打 hit, 推 push, 拉 pull; 捏 is pinching or kneading.

example.hanzi: 她捏了捏我的手。
example.pinyin: Tā niē le niē wǒ de shǒu.
example.english: She gave my hand a squeeze.
example.fact: 捏 is to pinch or to shape with the fingers: 捏饺子 (to crimp dumplings), 捏泥人 (to make clay figures), 捏造 (to fabricate). 捏一把汗 means to be anxious for someone, "pinching a handful of sweat."

examples.hanzi: 妈妈在厨房里捏饺子。
examples.pinyin: Māma zài chúfáng lǐ niē jiǎozi.
examples.english: Mom is shaping dumplings in the kitchen.

examples.hanzi: 他捏着鼻子走过了垃圾桶。
examples.pinyin: Tā niē zhe bízi zǒu guò le lājītǒng.
examples.english: He held his nose as he walked past the trash can.

components.note: 乛 (hook stroke) — the top-left bent stroke and dictionary radical; a stroke grouping with no meaning of its own.
一 (one) — the bottom bar. 卫 is simplified from 衛 (guard); Memory aid: a bar blocking a corner, a guard at the door.

example.hanzi: 请问，卫生间在哪里？
example.pinyin: Qǐngwèn, wèishēngjiān zài nǎlǐ?
example.english: Excuse me, where is the restroom?
example.fact: 卫 means to guard: 保卫, 自卫, 卫士 (guard). 卫生 is hygiene, and 卫生间 is the polite word for a restroom. 卫星 (satellite) is literally a "guard star."

examples.hanzi: 你好，请问卫生间怎么走？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ hǎo, qǐngwèn wèishēngjiān zěnme zǒu?
examples.english: Hello, how do I get to the restroom?

examples.hanzi: 饭前要先洗手，注意卫生。
examples.pinyin: Fàn qián yào xiān xǐshǒu, zhùyì wèishēng.
examples.english: Wash your hands before meals and pay attention to hygiene.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — a person resting on a mat under a roof: to lodge, as in 家 home, 安 peace. Also read xiǔ and xiù.
人 — the top is a roof shape over a dwelling, as in 宿舍; the lower part is not the tongue of 舌.

example.hanzi: 大学生通常住在宿舍里。
example.pinyin: Dàxuéshēng tōngcháng zhù zài sùshè lǐ.
example.english: College students usually live in dormitories.
example.fact: Oxford's oldest colleges, founded in the 13th century, originally housed students and tutors together in shared quarters organized much like monasteries, with communal dining halls and chapels. That residential college model, blending living space with study, went on to influence dormitory design at universities worldwide.

examples.hanzi: 我们宿舍有四个人,大家关系很好。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen sùshè yǒu sì gè rén, dàjiā guānxi hěn hǎo.
examples.english: There are four of us in our dorm, and we all get along well.

examples.hanzi: 宿舍晚上十一点关门,别回来太晚。
examples.pinyin: Sùshè wǎnshang shíyī diǎn guānmén, bié huílái tài wǎn.
examples.english: The dorm closes at eleven at night, so don't come back too late.

components.note: 广 (shelter) — a building, as in 店, 床, 度: hemp stalks drying in a shed. 麻 also gives sound to 磨 mó, 摩 mó and 魔 mó.
酉 (wine jar) — drink, as in 酒 liquor, 醒 sober.
卒 (zú) is a loose clue; it also sounds out 翠 cuì and 碎 suì.

example.hanzi: 手术前病人接受了麻醉。
example.pinyin: Shǒushù qián bìngrén jiēshòu le mázuì.
example.english: The patient received anesthesia before the surgery.
example.fact: On October 16, 1846, dentist William Morton administered ether anesthesia during a public surgery at Massachusetts General Hospital, in a room now nicknamed the 'Ether Dome.' The patient felt no pain, and news of the successful demonstration spread across the world within months, transforming surgery from an agonizing last resort into a survivable procedure.

examples.hanzi: 牙医给我打了麻醉,所以我不觉得疼。
examples.pinyin: Yáyī gěi wǒ dǎle mázuì, suǒyǐ wǒ bù juéde téng.
examples.english: The dentist gave me anesthesia, so I didn't feel any pain.

examples.hanzi: 手术需要全身麻醉。
examples.pinyin: Shǒushù xūyào quánshēn mázuì.
examples.english: The surgery requires general anesthesia.

meanings: to tell it as it is

components.note: 宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 字, 室: a house stocked with goods, so solid and real.
讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 说, 请, 谢; 话 is speech.
舌 (shé, tongue) fits the meaning (speaking) and is a loose sound clue for huà; also in 活 huó.
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 字, 室: a house stocked with goods, so solid and real.
讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 请, 谢, 话.
兑 (duì) is a loose sound clue for shuō; 兑 also sounds out 脱 tuō, 税 shuì and 悦 yuè.

example.hanzi: 我们应该实话实说，不要隐瞒。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen yīnggāi shíhuà shíshuō, bùyào yǐnmán.
example.english: We should tell the truth and not hide anything.
example.fact: Researchers at the University of Granada found in a 2012 thermal-imaging study that lying triggers a measurable temperature spike around the nose and a drop around the forehead, an effect nicknamed the 'Pinocchio effect.' The tiny, involuntary shift happens too fast for a liar to control, though it requires specialized cameras to detect.

examples.hanzi: 你实话实说吧,是不是你打碎的?
examples.pinyin: Nǐ shíhuà shíshuō ba, shì bú shì nǐ dǎsuì de?
examples.english: Tell it like it is: did you break it?

examples.hanzi: 他一向实话实说,从不拐弯抹角。
examples.pinyin: Tā yíxiàng shíhuà shíshuō, cóng bù guǎiwān-mòjiǎo.
examples.english: He always tells it as it is and never beats around the bush.

components.note: 纟 (silk, thread) — simplified 糸; thread is the classic fine thing, so 细 means thin, slender, then detailed — as in 线 line, 红 red.
艹 (grass) — plants and fungi; also in 草 grass, 菜 vegetable.
囷 (qūn) gives a close sound for jūn.

example.hanzi: 洗手可以减少细菌感染。
example.pinyin: Xǐshǒu kěyǐ jiǎnshǎo xìjūn gǎnrǎn.
example.english: Washing hands can reduce bacterial infection.
example.fact: Dutch tradesman Antonie van Leeuwenhoek was the first person to observe bacteria, using hand-ground microscope lenses in 1676 to see what he called 'animalcules' swimming in rainwater and plaque scraped from his own teeth. His detailed letters to the Royal Society laid the groundwork for microbiology two centuries before germ theory was formalized.

examples.hanzi: 生肉上有很多细菌,处理后要洗手。
examples.pinyin: Shēngròu shàng yǒu hěn duō xìjūn, chǔlǐ hòu yào xǐshǒu.
examples.english: Raw meat carries many germs, so wash your hands after handling it.

examples.hanzi: 酸奶里有对身体有益的细菌。
examples.pinyin: Suānnǎi lǐ yǒu duì shēntǐ yǒuyì de xìjūn.
examples.english: Yogurt contains bacteria that are good for the body.

components.note: 阝 (mound, left-side form of 阜 hill) — hills and places: 院, 阳, 陆; 队 is a group of people gathered together.
又 (hand) — two hands 又 stacked: hands joined in friendship.

example.hanzi: 他和队友配合得很好。
example.pinyin: Tā hé duìyǒu pèihé de hěn hǎo.
example.english: He and his teammates coordinated very well.
example.fact: In the 1980 Winter Olympics, a team of American college and amateur players — considered heavy underdogs — beat the dominant Soviet ice hockey squad 4-3 in a match later called the 'Miracle on Ice.' The US team went on to win the gold medal two days later against Finland.

examples.hanzi: 我的队友传球给我,我一脚射门。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de duìyǒu chuánqiú gěi wǒ, wǒ yì jiǎo shèmén.
examples.english: My teammate passed the ball to me and I took a shot.

examples.hanzi: 队友受伤了,我们只好换人。
examples.pinyin: Duìyǒu shòushāng le, wǒmen zhǐhǎo huànrén.
examples.english: A teammate got injured, so we had to substitute.

components.note: 亻 (person) — person radical — 仪 is the conduct of a person, as in 仪式 ceremony.
义 (yì) — near sound — 仪 is yí; 义 also sounds out 议 yì.
Four mouths 口 (vessels) with a dog 犬 guarding them — the traditional explanation; 器 is any vessel or tool, as in 武器 and 机器.

example.hanzi: 实验室里有很多精密仪器。
example.pinyin: Shíyànshì lǐ yǒu hěnduō jīngmì yíqì.
example.english: There are many precision instruments in the laboratory.
example.fact: The LIGO gravitational-wave detectors use laser beams bounced along 4-kilometer arms to measure distance changes smaller than one ten-thousandth the width of a proton. That extraordinary sensitivity let the instrument directly detect gravitational waves from colliding black holes for the first time in 2015.

examples.hanzi: 医院新买了一台昂贵的仪器。
examples.pinyin: Yīyuàn xīn mǎile yì tái ángguì de yíqì.
examples.english: The hospital bought a new expensive piece of equipment.

examples.hanzi: 学生们在老师的指导下学习使用仪器。
examples.pinyin: Xuéshengmen zài lǎoshī de zhǐdǎo xià xuéxí shǐyòng yíqì.
examples.english: Students learn to use the instruments under the teacher's guidance.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — three mouths: many goods and people speaking; hence products, quality, and to taste. Also in 品尝 and 作品.
口 (mouth) — tasting and speaking: 吃, 喝, 嗅; 味 is flavor.
未 (wèi) sounds exactly like 味; also 妹 mèi.

example.hanzi: 他对艺术很有品味。
example.pinyin: Tā duì yìshù hěn yǒu pǐnwèi.
example.english: He has great taste in art.
example.fact: Human tongues carry roughly 10,000 taste buds, each a cluster of receptor cells that gets replaced about every one to two weeks throughout life. That constant turnover means the tongue that tastes a favorite dish today is, cell for cell, not quite the same one that tasted it a month before.

examples.hanzi: 我想慢慢品味这杯茶。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng mànmàn pǐnwèi zhè bēi chá.
examples.english: I want to slowly savor this cup of tea.

examples.hanzi: 她穿衣服很有品味。
examples.pinyin: Tā chuān yīfu hěn yǒu pǐnwèi.
examples.english: She has great taste in clothes.

components.note: 木 (wood) — 标 first meant the tip of a tree, hence a mark or target; wood radical as in 树 tree, 板 board.
票 (piào) is the sound in traditional 標; same series 漂 piāo and 飘 piāo; simplified 标 now shows 示.
⺮ (bamboo) — ⺮ is bamboo, as in 笔, 筷, 箱; slips of bamboo were written on, so 签 is a slip or to sign.
佥 (qiān) — same sound — 签 is qiān; 佥 also sounds out 检 jiǎn and 脸 liǎn.

example.hanzi: 每个产品都贴着价格标签。
example.pinyin: Měi gè chǎnpǐn dōu tiē zhe jiàgé biāoqiān.
example.english: Every product has a price tag attached.
example.fact: The first retail barcode was scanned on June 26, 1974, at a Marsh supermarket in Troy, Ohio — a 10-pack of Wrigley's Juicy Fruit gum, which now sits in the Smithsonian. Barcodes and their price-tag labels went on to become standard on nearly every packaged product sold worldwide.

examples.hanzi: 这件衣服的标签还没有剪掉。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn yīfu de biāoqiān hái méiyǒu jiǎndiào.
examples.english: The tag on this garment hasn't been cut off yet.

examples.hanzi: 别给别人贴标签,每个人都不一样。
examples.pinyin: Bié gěi biéren tiē biāoqiān, měi gè rén dōu bù yíyàng.
examples.english: Don't label people; everyone is different.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — houses and shelter: 家, 安, 室; a guest is a person under your roof.
各 (gè) is a loose sound clue; same part in 路 lù, 洛 luò, 落 luò.
户 (door) — doors and houses, as in 所 and 扇: a room with a door.
方 (fāng) is a close sound clue for fáng; 方 also sounds out 放 fàng and 访 fǎng.

example.hanzi: 这家酒店的客房非常宽敞。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā jiǔdiàn de kèfáng fēicháng kuānchang.
example.english: This hotel's guest rooms are very spacious.
example.fact: The First World Hotel in Genting Highlands, Malaysia, once held the Guinness World Record for the most guest rooms in a single hotel, with over 7,300 rooms under one roof. That's roughly triple the room count of most of the largest hotels in Las Vegas.

examples.hanzi: 请问客房里有没有免费的无线网络?
examples.pinyin: Qǐngwèn kèfáng lǐ yǒu méiyǒu miǎnfèi de wúxiàn wǎngluò?
examples.english: Does the guest room have free Wi-Fi?

examples.hanzi: 我订了一间朝南的客房。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ dìngle yì jiān cháo nán de kèfáng.
examples.english: I booked a south-facing room.

components.note: 無 (traditional) — began as a person dancing with ornaments (same root as 舞). 'None' is a borrowed sense; 无 is an old variant of 無 and the shape does not explain it.
口 (mouth) — knowing is something you can say aloud; 口 sits in many speech words (问 ask, 告 tell).
矢 (shǐ, arrow) is only a loose sound clue today; the same 知 sound is in 智 zhì (wisdom).

example.hanzi: 他因为无知而做出错误的决定。
example.pinyin: Tā yīnwèi wúzhī ér zuòchū cuòwù de juédìng.
example.english: He made a wrong decision due to ignorance.
example.fact: Psychologists David Dunning and Justin Kruger described in a 1999 study what's now called the Dunning-Kruger effect: people with the least knowledge or skill in a domain often rate their own competence the highest, because the same ignorance that causes the mistakes also prevents them from recognizing the mistakes.

examples.hanzi: 无知并不可怕,可怕的是不愿意学习。
examples.pinyin: Wúzhī bìng bù kěpà, kěpà de shì bú yuànyì xuéxí.
examples.english: Ignorance isn't scary; what's scary is being unwilling to learn.

examples.hanzi: 他对这个问题一无所知,表现得很无知。
examples.pinyin: Tā duì zhège wèntí yì wú suǒ zhī, biǎoxiàn de hěn wúzhī.
examples.english: He knows nothing about this issue and comes across as ignorant.

components.note: 目 (eye) — sight, as in 看, 睛, 睡.
艮 (gèn) is a loose sound clue for yǎn; 艮 also sounds out 跟 gēn, 很 hěn and 根 gēn.
火 (fire) — fire above a person (儿 legs) — a person carrying fire gives light; 光 is bright and shining, as in 阳光, 时光.
儿 (legs, person) — the bottom 儿 is a walking person, seen also in 先, 兄, 元.

example.hanzi: 她挑选家具很有眼光。
example.pinyin: Tā tiāoxuǎn jiājù hěn yǒu yǎnguāng.
example.english: She has a good eye for choosing furniture.
example.fact: Birds of prey such as hawks and eagles have visual acuity estimated at two to eight times sharper than a human's, thanks to an unusually dense packing of photoreceptor cells in their retinas. A hawk circling high overhead can reportedly spot a small rodent moving in grass hundreds of meters below.

examples.hanzi: 老板很有眼光,早早买下了这家店。
examples.pinyin: Lǎobǎn hěn yǒu yǎnguāng, zǎozǎo mǎixiàle zhè jiā diàn.
examples.english: The boss has good judgment and bought this shop early.

examples.hanzi: 别用异样的眼光看着我。
examples.pinyin: Bié yòng yìyàng de yǎnguāng kànzhe wǒ.
examples.english: Don't look at me with such strange eyes.

components.note: 衣 (clothes; 衤 on the left) — the outer garment.
毛 (fur) — a fur coat worn outside: the outside, the surface, then to show.
木 (wood, tree) — wood radical — 格 first meant a wooden frame or lattice, hence "pattern, standard"; compare 树 tree, 板 board.
各 (gè) — same syllable, different tone — 格 is gé; 各 also sounds out 阁 gé and 胳 gē.

example.hanzi: 请填写这张表格。
example.pinyin: Qǐng tiánxiě zhè zhāng biǎogé.
example.english: Please fill out this form.
example.fact: When Dmitri Mendeleev published his periodic table in 1869, he left gaps for elements he believed must exist but hadn't yet been discovered, and predicted their properties from the table's pattern. Gallium, discovered six years later, matched his prediction so closely that it helped convince skeptical chemists the table was more than a filing system.

examples.hanzi: 申请签证需要填一张表格。
examples.pinyin: Shēnqǐng qiānzhèng xūyào tián yì zhāng biǎogé.
examples.english: Applying for a visa requires filling in a form.

examples.hanzi: 这个表格把全年的数据都列出来了。
examples.pinyin: Zhège biǎogé bǎ quánnián de shùjù dōu lièchūlái le.
examples.english: This table lists all the data for the whole year.

components.note: 王 (king) — three bars for heaven, people and earth joined by a vertical: the ruler who links them. As 玉 jade with its dot dropped it also marks jewels: 球, 玩.
囗 (enclosure) — borders and walls, as in 园 garden, 圆 round, 回 return; 囗 is the country's boundary.
玉 (jade) — treasure within the border; the traditional 國 had 或 (defended territory) inside.

example.hanzi: 这个王国有着悠久的历史。
example.pinyin: Zhège wángguó yǒuzhe yōujiǔ de lìshǐ.
example.english: This kingdom has a long history.
example.fact: Since the early 1970s, the Kingdom of Bhutan has officially tracked 'Gross National Happiness' alongside economic output, weighing factors like community vitality, culture, and environmental health in national policy decisions. It remains one of the only countries to enshrine a happiness index directly into its constitution.

examples.hanzi: 这个小王国有一位善良的国王。
examples.pinyin: Zhège xiǎo wángguó yǒu yí wèi shànliáng de guówáng.
examples.english: This little kingdom has a kind king.

examples.hanzi: 孩子们在玩具王国里玩得很开心。
examples.pinyin: Háizimen zài wánjù wángguó lǐ wán de hěn kāixīn.
examples.english: The children are having a great time in the toy kingdom.

components.note: 广 (building) — 广 is a building or roof, as in 店, 床, 库; 废 is a ruined building, then discarded.
发 (fā) — loose hint — 废 is fèi, close in sound to 发 fā.

example.hanzi: 这台旧电脑已经废了。
example.pinyin: Zhè tái jiù diànnǎo yǐjīng fèi le.
example.english: This old computer is already useless.
example.fact: 废 is usually seen inside compounds such as 废话 (pointless talk), 废物 (waste, or a useless person) and 废除 (to abolish). Used alone as an adjective it is blunt and colloquial, like saying something is 'dead' or 'junk'.

examples.hanzi: 这些旧报纸都是废纸。
examples.pinyin: Zhèxiē jiù bàozhǐ dōu shì fèizhǐ.
examples.english: These old newspapers are all waste paper.

examples.hanzi: 这个计划被取消了，等于废了。
examples.pinyin: Zhège jìhuà bèi qǔxiāo le, děngyú fèi le.
examples.english: This plan was cancelled, so it is as good as scrapped.

components.note: 大 (big) — a front-facing person with arms and legs spread wide: big. As radical, 大 is in 天 sky, 太 too much, 夫 man.
亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do. 便 is a person adjusting things 更 to make them convenient (traditional explanation).

example.hanzi: 医生检查了病人的大便样本。
example.pinyin: Yīshēng jiǎnchá le bìngrén de dàbiàn yàngběn.
example.english: The doctor examined the patient's stool sample.
example.fact: A 2013 study found that dung beetles use the Milky Way as a compass, rolling their dung balls in straight lines at night by orienting to the band of starlight overhead. They were the first animal shown to navigate by the galaxy rather than the moon or individual stars.

examples.hanzi: 宝宝今天的大便很正常,不用担心。
examples.pinyin: Bǎobao jīntiān de dàbiàn hěn zhèngcháng, bú yòng dānxīn.
examples.english: The baby's stool is normal today, so no need to worry.

examples.hanzi: 医生让他每天早上记录大便的情况。
examples.pinyin: Yīshēng ràng tā měitiān zǎoshang jìlù dàbiàn de qíngkuàng.
examples.english: The doctor asked him to record his bowel movements every morning.

components.note: 彳 (step, walk) — 彳 is the left-step radical, as in 行, 径, 德; 往 is going toward.
王 (wáng) — near sound — 往 is wǎng, same syllable with a different tone.
巾 (cloth) — cloth and clothing, as in 布 cloth, 带 belt, 帽 hat; 常 first meant a long skirt (裳 cháng).
尚 (shàng) is a loose sound clue for cháng; 尚 also sounds out 堂 táng and 掌 zhǎng.

example.hanzi: 他往常都很早起床。
example.pinyin: Tā wǎngcháng dōu hěn zǎo qǐchuáng.
example.english: He usually gets up early.
example.fact: French researcher Michel Siffre spent two months living in a cave in 1962 with no clocks or daylight cues, tracking only how his body felt. His internal clock drifted to a day length of about 24.5 hours, part of the early evidence that the human circadian rhythm runs slightly longer than a calendar day.

examples.hanzi: 今天比往常冷,多穿点衣服。
examples.pinyin: Jīntiān bǐ wǎngcháng lěng, duō chuān diǎn yīfu.
examples.english: It's colder than usual today, so wear more clothes.

examples.hanzi: 和往常一样,他六点就起床了。
examples.pinyin: Hé wǎngcháng yíyàng, tā liù diǎn jiù qǐchuáng le.
examples.english: As usual, he got up at six.

components.note: 毛 (hair) — a picture of a tuft of hair or fur; used in 毛巾 and 毛病 (a flaw).
衣 (clothes) — a picture of a coat with a collar and sleeves. As a radical it is 衤 on the left: 裤 trousers, 衬 shirt, 被 quilt.

example.hanzi: 冬天她总是穿毛衣。
example.pinyin: Dōngtiān tā zǒngshì chuān máoyī.
example.english: In winter she always wears a sweater.
example.fact: Merino wool fibers can absorb up to roughly 30 percent of their own weight in moisture before feeling wet to the touch, while still trapping air to insulate against cold. That combination of warmth and breathability is why merino sweaters are prized for both winter wear and high-exertion outdoor gear.

examples.hanzi: 奶奶织了一件红色的毛衣给我。
examples.pinyin: Nǎinai zhīle yí jiàn hóngsè de máoyī gěi wǒ.
examples.english: Grandma knitted me a red sweater.

examples.hanzi: 这件毛衣洗过以后缩水了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn máoyī xǐguo yǐhòu suōshuǐ le.
examples.english: This sweater shrank after being washed.

components.note: 亲 (qīn) keeps the sound part of the traditional 親, which also had 见; it also gives 新 xīn and 薪 xīn, so qīn/xīn is a series.
灬 (fire) — 灬 is fire at the bottom, as in 点, 照, 熟; 热 is heat.

example.hanzi: 老朋友见面格外亲热。
example.pinyin: Lǎo péngyou jiànmiàn géwài qīnrè.
example.english: Old friends were especially affectionate when they met.
example.fact: Physical affection such as hugging triggers the release of oxytocin, a hormone first isolated in 1906 that lowers stress hormones and blood pressure in both the giver and receiver of the embrace. Oxytocin release also spikes during childbirth and breastfeeding, which is why it's often nicknamed the 'bonding hormone.'

examples.hanzi: 小猫亲热地靠在我脚边。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎo māo qīnrè de kào zài wǒ jiǎobiān.
examples.english: The kitten snuggled up affectionately by my feet.

examples.hanzi: 两个姐妹亲热地聊了一整晚。
examples.pinyin: Liǎng gè jiěmèi qīnrè de liáole yì zhěng wǎn.
examples.english: The two sisters chatted warmly all night.

components.note: 攵 (tap, strike) — hand with stick, as in 教, 收, 改: to drive away, set free.
方 (fāng) is a close sound clue for fàng; 方 also in 房 fáng and 访 fǎng.
大 (big) — a front-facing person with arms and legs spread wide: big. As radical, 大 is in 天 sky, 太 too much, 夫 man.

example.hanzi: 请把这张图片放大一些。
example.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ zhè zhāng túpiàn fàngdà yīxiē.
example.english: Please enlarge this picture a bit.
example.fact: The Hubble Space Telescope, launched in 1990, has captured images of galaxies more than 13 billion light-years away by gathering and magnifying faint light that left its source before the Earth even existed. Its Deep Field images, made by staring at a single patch of seemingly empty sky for days, revealed thousands of previously invisible galaxies.

examples.hanzi: 这个图片太小了,能不能放大?
examples.pinyin: Zhège túpiàn tài xiǎo le, néng bù néng fàngdà?
examples.english: This picture is too small; can you enlarge it?

examples.hanzi: 他用放大镜看那枚旧邮票。
examples.pinyin: Tā yòng fàngdàjìng kàn nà méi jiù yóupiào.
examples.english: He looked at the old stamp through a magnifying glass.

components.note: 日 (sun) — sun, light and time: 明 bright, 晴 clear, 时 time; stars are points of light.
生 (shēng) is a loose sound hint for xīng (-ng ending); also in 性 xìng, 姓 xìng.
阝 (mound, left-side form of 阜 hill) — relates to hills, walls and places, as in 院 courtyard, 阳 sun-side, 陆 land; fits 际 as a boundary.
示 (shì) is only a loose sound hint — traditional 際 used 祭 (jì), and simplification swapped in 示.

example.hanzi: 这部电影讲述了星际旅行的故事。
example.pinyin: Zhè bù diànyǐng jiǎngshù le xīngjì lǚxíng de gùshì.
example.english: This movie tells a story about interstellar travel.
example.fact: Voyager 1, launched by NASA in 1977 to study Jupiter and Saturn, became the first human-made object to cross into interstellar space in 2012, roughly 11 billion miles from the sun. It's still transmitting data today, powered by a slowly decaying plutonium generator expected to run out sometime in the 2030s.

examples.hanzi: 他最喜欢看星际战争的电影。
examples.pinyin: Tā zuì xǐhuan kàn xīngjì zhànzhēng de diànyǐng.
examples.english: He loves watching movies about interstellar wars.

examples.hanzi: 科学家想建造星际飞船。
examples.pinyin: Kēxuéjiā xiǎng jiànzào xīngjì fēichuán.
examples.english: Scientists want to build an interstellar spaceship.

components.note: 木 (tree) — 杰 is simplified from 傑; a tall tree makes a handy picture for an outstanding person standing tall.
凵 (open pit) — oldest form shows a foot stepping out of a pit or cave: to go out, come out.

example.hanzi: 她是一位杰出的科学家。
example.pinyin: Tā shì yī wèi jiéchū de kēxuéjiā.
example.english: She is an outstanding scientist.
example.fact: Marie Curie remains the only person to win Nobel Prizes in two different sciences — Physics in 1903 for her work on radioactivity, and Chemistry in 1911 for discovering the elements polonium and radium. She did much of that pioneering research in a converted shed, without the safety equipment that her own findings would later make standard.

examples.hanzi: 他是一位杰出的画家,作品卖到了国外。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì yí wèi jiéchū de huàjiā, zuòpǐn màidàole guówài.
examples.english: He is an outstanding painter whose works have sold abroad.

examples.hanzi: 这位学生的表现非常杰出。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi xuésheng de biǎoxiàn fēicháng jiéchū.
examples.english: This student's performance is remarkable.

components.note: 亻 (person) — a person bowing low; also in 他 he, 们 plural.
氐 (dī) gives the exact sound; it also sounds out 底 dǐ and 抵 dǐ.
讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 说, 请, 谢.
周 (zhōu) is a loose sound clue for diào/tiáo; 周 also in 凋 diāo.

example.hanzi: 他为人低调，很少接受采访。
example.pinyin: Tā wéirén dīdiào, hěn shǎo jiēshòu cǎifǎng.
example.english: He keeps a low profile and rarely gives interviews.
example.fact: Eighteenth-century scientist Henry Cavendish, who discovered hydrogen and precisely measured the density of the Earth, was so famously reclusive that he reportedly communicated with his own servants through written notes rather than speak to them directly. Much of his unpublished research on electricity was only discovered and recognized decades after his death.

examples.hanzi: 他穿着低调,没有人认出他是明星。
examples.pinyin: Tā chuānzhe dīdiào, méiyǒu rén rèn chū tā shì míngxīng.
examples.english: He dressed low-key, so nobody recognized him as a star.

examples.hanzi: 这家餐厅装修得很低调,但菜很好吃。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā cāntīng zhuāngxiū de hěn dīdiào, dàn cài hěn hǎochī.
examples.english: This restaurant is decorated in a low-key style, but the food is delicious.

components.note: 耳 (ear) — the left part and radical, as in 听 listen. 耶 mostly writes foreign names (耶稣 Jesus), so the ear is only a shape hint.
阝 (city) — the right part, as in 都 and 那. It does not give the sound here. Memory aid: an ear in a foreign city hearing a new name.
鱼 (fish) — the old 魯 had fish on top; the meaning 'foolish, rash' is later and not about fish. 鲁 is mostly the state and surname Lu.
日 (sun) — at the bottom (from older 白). Memory aid: a fish gaping in the sun is dazed — hence foolish, rash.

example.hanzi: 他被耶鲁大学录取了。
example.pinyin: Tā bèi Yēlǔ Dàxué lùqǔ le.
example.english: He was admitted to Yale University.
example.fact: Founded in 1701, Yale is the third-oldest institution of higher education in the United States. Its Beinecke Rare Book Library holds one of only about 50 surviving complete copies of the Gutenberg Bible, the first major book printed in Europe with movable type.

examples.hanzi: 我表哥去耶鲁大学读研究生了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ biǎogē qù Yēlǔ dàxué dú yánjiūshēng le.
examples.english: My cousin went to Yale University for graduate school.

examples.hanzi: 耶鲁在美国的东部,是一所很有名的学校。
examples.pinyin: Yēlǔ zài Měiguó de dōngbù, shì yì suǒ hěn yǒumíng de xuéxiào.
examples.english: Yale is in the eastern US and is a very famous school.

components.note: 木 (wood) — palm trees; also in 树 tree, 林 forest.
宗 (zōng) gives the exact sound; it also sounds out 踪 zōng and 综 zōng.
木 (wood) — trees; also in 树 tree, 林 forest.
闾 (lǘ) gives the sound; it contains 吕 lǚ, which also sounds out 侣 lǚ and 铝 lǚ.

example.hanzi: 海边种着很多棕榈树。
example.pinyin: Hǎibiān zhòng zhe hěnduō zōnglǚ shù.
example.english: Many palm trees are planted by the seaside.
example.fact: Coconut palms produce seeds so buoyant and salt-tolerant that they can float across entire oceans and still germinate after drifting for over 100 days at sea. That built-in seaworthiness is how coconut palms spread naturally to remote tropical islands long before humans ever planted them there.

examples.hanzi: 这条街两边种满了棕榈树。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tiáo jiē liǎngbiān zhòngmǎnle zōnglǘ shù.
examples.english: Both sides of this street are lined with palm trees.

examples.hanzi: 棕榈叶可以编成帽子。
examples.pinyin: Zōnglǘ yè kěyǐ biānchéng màozi.
examples.english: Palm leaves can be woven into hats.

components.note: 阝 on the left is 阜 (steps, hill) — as in 院, 阳, 阴: 除 first meant palace steps; to step away, remove.
余 (yú) is a loose sound clue for chú; 余 also in 涂 tú, 途 tú and 徐 xú.
此 (cǐ) is a sound clue for 紫 zǐ, 雌 cí and 些 xiē; as a word it means "this".
之 (of, go) — oldest form is a foot leaving a starting line: "to go". Now it is a literary particle meaning "of" or "it".
夕 (evening) — the left part, the time-of-day family as in 夜, 多, 梦. Memory aid: things done at night are outside the ordinary.
卜 (divination) — Dictionary story: night 夕 divination 卜, strange and 'outside'. A hedged mnemonic: 外面 outside, 另外 in addition.

example.hanzi: 除此之外，他还学过法语。
example.pinyin: Chú cǐ zhī wài, tā hái xué guò Fǎyǔ.
example.english: Besides this, he has also studied French.
example.fact: The Rosetta Stone, carved in 196 BC, records the same royal decree in three scripts: Egyptian hieroglyphs, Egyptian demotic, and ancient Greek. Because scholars could already read Greek, the stone gave French scholar Jean-François Champollion the key that let him decipher hieroglyphic writing in 1822, unlocking millennia of Egyptian history.

examples.hanzi: 除此之外,我们没有别的问题了。
examples.pinyin: Chú cǐ zhī wài, wǒmen méiyǒu bié de wèntí le.
examples.english: Other than this, we have no further questions.

examples.hanzi: 这家酒店有游泳池,除此之外,还有健身房。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā jiǔdiàn yǒu yóuyǒngchí, chú cǐ zhī wài, hái yǒu jiànshēnfáng.
examples.english: This hotel has a pool, and in addition, a gym.

components.note: 心 (heart) — feelings: 想, 思, 感, 怕; 急 is a heart in a hurry. The top is a variant of 及 (jí, reach), the same sound as in 级 and 极.
讠 (speech, from 言) — marks talk and questions, as in 说, 请, 问; 诊 is a doctor questioning and examining.
㐱 (zhěn) gives the sound exactly: 诊 zhěn, also in 疹 zhěn.
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 安, 字: a room under the roof.
至 (zhì, arrive) is a loose sound clue for shì; it fits the meaning: where one arrives inside the house.

example.hanzi: 他被送进了急诊室。
example.pinyin: Tā bèi sòng jìn le jízhěnshì.
example.english: He was rushed into the emergency room.
example.fact: Trauma surgeon R Adams Cowley popularized the concept of the 'golden hour' in the 1970s, the idea that a severely injured patient's odds of survival are highest if they reach definitive care within about 60 minutes of injury. The concept reshaped how emergency rooms and ambulance systems prioritize speed for trauma cases.

examples.hanzi: 救护车把他送到了急诊室。
examples.pinyin: Jiùhùchē bǎ tā sòngdàole jíchěnshì.
examples.english: The ambulance took him to the emergency room.

examples.hanzi: 晚上急诊室里总是有很多人。
examples.pinyin: Wǎnshang jíchěnshì lǐ zǒngshì yǒu hěn duō rén.
examples.english: There are always lots of people in the emergency room at night.

components.note: 比 (compare) — two people side by side, one lined up with the other; to compare.
牛 (ox) — cattle and animals, as in 物 thing, 牧 herd, 牺 sacrifice: 特 first meant a bull, then special.
寺 (sì) is only a loose sound clue for tè; 寺 also in 诗 shī and 持 chí.

example.hanzi: 一个字节等于八个比特。
example.pinyin: Yī gè zìjié děngyú bā gè bǐtè.
example.english: One byte equals eight bits.
example.fact: Mathematician and engineer Claude Shannon coined the term 'bit,' short for 'binary digit,' in his 1948 paper 'A Mathematical Theory of Communication,' which founded the field of information theory. His framework for measuring information in bits underlies essentially all digital communication and storage used today.

examples.hanzi: 电脑里的信息是用比特来计算的。
examples.pinyin: Diànnǎo lǐ de xìnxī shì yòng bǐtè lái jìsuàn de.
examples.english: Information in computers is measured in bits.

examples.hanzi: 这个文件只有几百个比特。
examples.pinyin: Zhège wénjiàn zhǐyǒu jǐ bǎi gè bǐtè.
examples.english: This file is only a few hundred bits.
